title: What Holds Tech Week's 1,500 Events Together
summary: A steady content feed lets attendees experience the parts they couldn't attend in person. For planners running multi-venue or community-driven events, it's a case for treating content as the infrastructure, not just the recap.

title: The CSR Activity That Started With a Handmade Birthday Card
summary: Jordan Lacey started Light the Candle at 17 to make birthday cards for foster children in her community. Now in the events industry, she is creating CSR activities that can be done anywhere.

title: After Informa-Clarion, Who Buys Next?
summary: About $10 billion in trade show deals in six months, plus private equity firms looking to build on new platforms, means Informa-Clarion is unlikely to be the last big move. Smaller organizers and event tech companies look like the next targets.

title: Informa's $3 Billion Clarion Deal Set to Reshape Events Industry
summary: Informa was already the world’s largest exhibition organizer. Its nearly $3 billion acquisition of Clarion Events raises a bigger question: What happens when one company controls roughly 1,000 B2B brands and gains even greater leverage with the destinations, venues, suppliers, and exhibitors it does business with?

title: Why Planners Are Turning to the World's Safest Region for Annual Meetings and Incentives
summary: Long-haul destinations have long been prized for their novelty, but they are now equally valued as safe havens from global unrest. Find out how Sydney, a well-known bucket-list destination, is helping to shorten the distance for planners looking to give their attendees the experience of a lifetime in the world’s safest region.

title: New Industry Community Will Focus on Seasoned Pros
summary: The industry devotes a lot of energy to mentoring the younger generation. APEX Event Network is betting that the most experienced planners need resources to continue their professional development, too.

title: Can AI Source Your Next Meeting Destination?
summary: An industry built on the power of human relationships is confronting machine-produced site recommendations. What if AI gets the answer wrong?

title: Private Equity's $6 Billion Bet on Trade Shows
summary: Private equity is paying top dollar for trade shows on the theory that AI can't replace a show floor. PE-owned organizers grew 11.4% last year, well ahead of most rivals, but Informa still dominates the top of the list after buying its way to 30% growth.

title: 6 Lessons to Navigate the Future of Events
summary: The planners who do well in 2027 won't be the ones doing more. They'll be the ones who know what to protect, what to verify, and when to say no.

title: Can Your Next Human Hire Beat an AI Agent?
summary: If meeting planners start managing AI agents, the case for adding headcount is about to get harder to make.
